name: Mercantilism
summary: Mercantilism was the economic doctrine and practice of early modern Europe that treated national wealth as a matter of power. States sought a surplus of exports over imports, protected home manufactures with high tariffs, held monopolies and colonies, and regulated trade and industry. Trade was seen as zero-sum, and wealth, population and military strength reinforced one another.
scope: The mainstream European mercantilism of the 16th to 18th centuries as documented in Thomas Mun's England's Treasure by Forraign Trade (England) and Colbert's policies (France, Colbertism). It excludes later economic nationalism such as List's and the American System, and neo-mercantilist policies today. Most statements postdate the doctrine, so many answers are inferred.

furtherReading.title: Thomas Mun, England's Treasure by Forraign Trade (excerpt)
furtherReading.note: A founding English statement of the trade-balance idea, in modernized spelling.

furtherReading.title: Colbertism
furtherReading.note: The French state-directed form of mercantilism under Louis XIV.

keyFigures.name: Thomas Mun
keyFigures.role: English merchant whose England's Treasure by Forraign Trade became the archetype of mercantilist writing.

keyFigures.name: Jean-Baptiste Colbert
keyFigures.role: Finance minister of Louis XIV whose policies gave mercantilism its most identifiable form.

sources.title: Mercantilism
sources.author: Wikipedia

sources.author: Thomas Mun, via Fordham Modern History Sourcebook
sources.usedFor: Selling more abroad than is consumed, treasure inflow, protection of trade by power, trade as the sinews of war.

sources.title: Colbertism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: State manufactures, monopolies, regulation, tariffs, colonies, navy and taxation under Colbert.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed; state care for the poor was limited and the era's policy focused on trade and power, so adherents would not demand it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Many mercantilists held that workers should be kept near subsistence so they stay industrious and exports stay cheap.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The state was meant to steer the economy as it steered diplomacy, though British mercantilism relied heavily on merchants.

public-ownership.rationale: Colbert set up state-sponsored manufactures and chartered monopolies, but outright public ownership of utilities was not the program.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Colbert tried and failed to tax the nobility, but taxing wealth for redistribution was not a mercantilist aim; adherents are split.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: guilds were regulated by the state and wages were to be held low, so independent labour organizing did not fit.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: property mattered to merchants, but the state overrode it through monopolies, prohibitions and regulation for national wealth.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Colbert imposed detailed quality rules, inspections and fines, and chartered companies were state-regulated monopolies.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the view that extra income, leisure or education encouraged idleness among workers.

worker-ownership.rationale: Anachronistic; mercantilists favoured merchant and state-chartered enterprise, not worker-owned firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: Colbert's regime enforced rules with inspectors and spies, and state power served national strength.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; a state-power, population-and-order outlook leans against it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed and anachronistic; no clear position follows from the doctrine.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred from Colbert serving an absolute monarch, though British mercantilism was limited by Parliament and common law.

state-harmful.rationale: Mercantilism is the use of state power to build national wealth and strength; the state is its instrument.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no stated position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Wealth was pursued as a means of national power, and navies and armies were tied to trade rivalry.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's moral regulation.

decide-locally.rationale: Mercantilism is a national project; Colbert sought to unify the fragmented internal customs under the crown.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; era's penal thinking was punitive.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: a large population was seen as wealth, favouring family formation and conventional order.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the era's conventions.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the view that population is a source of national wealth and power.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred: states of the era had established churches and public religion; no stated mercantilist position.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Colonial and slave-trade systems were integral to mercantilist empires, which makes remedies unlikely.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred from the nation-state and national-power focus.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred: policy worked through existing crowns, parliaments and chartered bodies.

reduce-immigration.rationale: A large population was seen as a source of wealth, and Colbert recruited skilled foreign artisans, so adherents tended to welcome numbers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: trade is zero-sum rivalry between sovereign states, leaving no room for binding supranational bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Mercantilists saw trade as zero-sum and used high tariffs and controls; Adam Smith's critique targeted exactly this.

nation-first.rationale: The state steers the economy to build national power at the expense of rivals.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anachronistic; wars were fought for trade and power, not human rights.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from state control of trade, people and colonies for national advantage.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: wealth and power accumulation was the goal, with no environmental limit in view.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the priority on national wealth and output.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Mercantilists promoted manufactures and skills but did not make a general claim about technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the aim of national strength and self-sufficiency.

revolution-justified.rationale: Inferred: mercantilism worked through crowns and established states.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from state officials such as Colbert directing economic policy.

central-planning.rationale: Heavy regulation in France shows state direction, but black markets and limited enforcement were recognized and no one planned production wholesale.

socialized-markets.rationale: Anachronistic; mercantilists backed merchant and state-chartered firms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; Colbert shifted toward indirect taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; no support in the sources.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic and at odds with keeping workers industrious.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: High tariffs, especially on manufactured goods, were nearly universal under mercantilism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Colbert founded and subsidized state manufactures and trading companies in strategic sectors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred: policy favoured large chartered monopolies and state manufactures over small-owner dispersion.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Money, and bullion especially, was the measure of national wealth, and wage labour was assumed.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: the state's control of money and credit served national power.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from state-regulated guilds and chartered bodies, though wage-setting by bargaining was not the form.

one-party-rule.rationale: Anachronistic; not part of the doctrine.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Colbert served Louis XIV and mercantilism developed within early modern monarchies.

democracy-best.rationale: Anachronistic; mercantilist states were monarchies or oligarchic parliaments.

direct-votes.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the era's institutions.

workers-councils.rationale: Anachronistic and opposed to keeping workers subordinate.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from the unitary national power project.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical order of the era.

political-violence-never.rationale: Wars and imperial rivalry were integral to the doctrine, though private political violence is not discussed.

war-builds-character.rationale: Mercantilists valued war as an instrument of power, not as character formation; adherents have no clear position.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from the era's established churches.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not a theme of mercantilist writing.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: defence and trade protection were state functions, as Mun's call for power to protect trade suggests.

military-superiority.rationale: Mercantilism was closely tied to warfare and imperial rivalry; Mun called trade the sinews of war.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not an ethnic doctrine; policy cared about population size and skills, including foreign artisans.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Anachronistic and opposed to the era's view of a harmonious order of ranks.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred from keeping workers near subsistence.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Colonies existed to supply materials and markets for the mother country.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Colonies were seen as assets of the mother country.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred: national self-interest was explicit, and Mun praised the merchant's profession.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from the subordination of private interests to national power.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Anachronistic; nature was a source of raw materials.

limit-population.rationale: A large population was seen as a source of labor, markets and soldiers.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Mercantilists promoted manufacturing as a source of wealth.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; adherents promoted manufactures but also rigid regulation.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis for a position.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from human officials directing policy.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from state surveillance and control.

restore-past-order.rationale: Mercantilists were pursuing national wealth and power, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Viner saw it as a common-sense system; writers addressed single problems instead of a theory.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred: pursuit of power did not require consistency of means.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred from the push for manufacture and trade.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Colbert's manufactures involved detailed specialization and regulation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Workers were kept near subsistence and distribution followed rank.

production-for-use.rationale: Production was aimed at exports and national power.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred: merchant profit was seen as a national benefit, as Mun praised the merchant.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anachronistic and opposed to keeping workers subordinate.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Mercantilists saw trade rivalry as leading to war but embraced it rather than blaming a system.

taxation-theft.rationale: Colbert raised state revenue through indirect taxes and the state's fiscal power was central.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from detailed state regulation of manufacture and trade.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Inferred: national interest outranked private rights.

conscription.rationale: Population was valued partly as soldiers, and states built armies and navies.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: states retained and recruited people as national assets.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred; states used business tools but were not run as exit-based firms.

organic-representation.rationale: Guilds and chartered bodies had roles, but representation was not a mercantilist theme.

total-state.rationale: Colbert regulated extensively but not every area; British mercantilism was limited by Parliament and common law.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Colonies supplied metals and raw materials, and imperial rivalry was central.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred: states of the era were moving to offices and law.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of the doctrine at home, though colonial slave labor was, which makes this a split.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilist writers, so no position follows from the doctrine.

single-common-good.rationale: Mercantilists framed a national interest but also served particular merchant interests, as critics like Ekelund argue.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilist writers, so no position follows from the doctrine.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Anachronistic and against the era's hierarchy.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Early writers stressed bullion; later ones stressed circulating money to stimulate trade, so adherents are split.

economic-freedom.rationale: The state was meant to steer the economy, with prohibitions, monopolies and tariffs.

rule-by-example.rationale: Colbert relied on rules, inspections and fines.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; sovereign states used force for trade advantage.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilist writers, so no position follows from the doctrine.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the view that idleness should be discouraged.

class-collaboration.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of a common national interest across ranks.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not a theme of mercantilist writing; inferred as opposed.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred from state rivalry and colonial domination.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred from national solidarity over international class.

ban-interest.rationale: Mun's merchant outlook assumes credit and exchange, and the Bank of England arose in this era.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Inferred; critics such as Ekelund framed it as rent-seeking, but adherents held it served the nation.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Colbert recruited foreign artisans; assimilation was not a stated aim.

elite-replacement.rationale: Anachronistic conspiracy claim; no basis in the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the doctrine's era and institutions.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed as a mission to spread a political system.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilist writers, so no position follows from the doctrine.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state power focus.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The doctrine is an active state steering trade, manufacture and colonies.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilist writers, so no position follows from the doctrine.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Inferred from hierarchy of ranks and colonial slavery.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the doctrine's era and institutions.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Colonies were assets of the mother country.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilist writers, so no position follows from the doctrine.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilist writers, so no position follows from the doctrine.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilist writers, so no position follows from the doctrine.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred: states under rivalry strengthened armies and navies.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mercantilist writers presented their claims as sound objective reasoning about trade; the question postdates the doctrine, so inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mun says to sell more to strangers yearly than we consume of theirs, and the favourable balance of trade is the central mercantilist aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Mercantilists valued a large population as a source of wealth and power, but also supported expulsions in practice (such as of Huguenots by others); split and unaddressed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Mercantilism treated trade as zero-sum and war and colonies as tools of wealth; Mun calls trade the sinews of war and the state used force freely.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Trade was seen as zero-sum competition between nations, though the goal was national power rather than progress; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Absolutist states of the era suppressed opposition freely, and parties did not yet exist; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Mercantilist states relied on monopolies and royal regulation of trade, with no concern for freedom from arbitrary power; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Colbertism relied on strong centralised royal authority directing the economy, favouring concentrated power; English practice was more mixed.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine served established monarchies and merchants and opposed revolution; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Policy aimed at national wealth and power, with low wages favoured to keep exports competitive, not at the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; mercantilism focused on trade and state power, so adherents have no clear view on public housing sales.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the mercantilist wish to keep workers industrious and export costs low, and from state regulation of labor and industry.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Mercantilists generally saw a large population as a source of wealth and power, so they did not blame population for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed; mercantilists favored national unity and power but did not frame the question as diversity versus cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, monarchical and state-directed setting of mercantilism, in which offices went by patronage or purchase.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the strong-state, crown-directed setting of mercantilist practice, in which the sovereign's power took priority over legal limits.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Colbert's state regulation of markets and mercantilist concern for grain supply support price ceilings, though this is inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from crown licensing and censorship of the press in mercantilist states; parties did not yet exist, so this is by analogy.

party-commands-army.rationale: In mercantilist states the army answered to the crown and state, and parties did not exist; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Mercantilists valued population growth and often welcomed skilled immigrants, so they would not want long waits; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a crown-run state staffed by gentry and officers who held office as rank and reward, not as ordinary-wage service.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Parties as modern organizations did not exist and the doctrine is silent; inferred indifference.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from the zero-sum view of trade and the aim of national power: handing trade control to a shared body would give away the means of national strength.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Colbertism ran through a monarch who commanded the forces and appointed ministers such as Colbert himself, and Mun treats trade as protected by the sovereign's power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not a doctrine of mercantilism; inferred from the states it served, where established churches were governed by crown-appointed bishops.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred: policy was made by lay ministers and merchants pursuing state power and wealth, not by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Mun calls trade the sinews of war and wealth and power reinforce each other, so adherents back their own state in rivalry between powers.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The doctrine concerns trade and state power, not culture; any censorship by mercantilist states was not part of the theory.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: mercantilist states were mostly monarchies with rulers serving for life, and Colbert served decades; term limits were foreign to them.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: officials served at the crown's pleasure and were answerable upward, not to voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Mun says trade must be protected by power and Colbert built a navy and colonies, so adherents would keep military reach abroad; alliances themselves are not addressed (inferred).

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine left property and markets to merchants and landowners under state regulation, so a ban on renting is inferred to be foreign to it.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred: mercantilism tied national wealth to state military power, and Colbert built standing forces and a navy rather than relying on a citizen militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: mercantilists prized manufactures, trade and towns as sources of national wealth, so they would not rank rural life above city life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed; mercantilist states were dynastic and competitive, and adherents had no settled view on reunifying divided peoples.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; merchant writers like Mun valued practical commercial knowledge, but the state also relied on learned officials, so adherents were split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred: European mercantilist states ran colonies on the assumption of their own superiority and did not treat other societies as equals.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred: early modern states used capital punishment widely, and nothing in mercantilism opposes it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; mercantilism had no view on school curricula, and the era left such teaching to church and family, so adherents would not endorse it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; in the era schooling was religious and creation accounts were the norm, so adherents would likely accept them in schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Anachronistic; early modern states policed morals and obscenity, and mercantilism offers no objection.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; Colbert welcomed skilled foreign artisans and mercantilists wanted a large population, but rules of birth citizenship were not an issue for the doctrine.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred: Colbertist France favoured centralised state administration in one language and did not support minority languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred: Colbertist regulation was uniform and state-directed, and the doctrine gives no ground for exempting groups from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred: mercantilism favoured detailed state regulation of trade and industry for national ends, not individual eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; mercantilist states treated credit and the claims of creditor powers as tools of national wealth, so wholesale cancellation is inferred as unwelcome.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: mercantilists sought national power through state-directed trade and monopolies within existing property relations, not a transformation of ownership.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Mercantilism was practised by monarchies such as Colbert's France, which kept constitutional authority with the crown; inferred from that.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Colbert regulated industry and trade closely and subordinated individual economic liberty to state wealth and power; political freedom is inferred to rank below this.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Mercantilists saw trade and wealth as zero-sum, so giving away national wealth to foreigners would weaken the state; inferred from that view.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Mun's view that trade is protected by power and wealth is the sinews of war, which favors self-reliant military strength.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Mercantilist states were monarchies, and the doctrine assumes a sovereign directing national policy; inferred from that.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Anachronistic; mercantilists wanted the state to control money and treasure for national power, so an independent bank is inferred as unwelcome.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred: territory, colonies and trade positions were sources of wealth and power that mercantilist states fought to keep.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred: mercantilists subordinated private enterprise to national wealth and power through monopolies and regulation, though they did not state this as a theory of property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine predates the Soviet Union and gives no basis for classifying it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine prized output, trade and national power, so restraint on uncertain risks is inferred to rank below them.

collective-defense.rationale: Mercantilist states made and broke alliances according to commercial and strategic advantage, so binding mutual defense is not part of the doctrine.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Colonies and conquered territory were sources of wealth and markets, so mercantilists did not treat annexation without consent as unlawful; inferred from the colonial system.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from the strong-state outlook of Colbertism, in which the crown directed economic and civil life; the doctrine itself is not about religion.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; mercantilist states were run by monarchs and ministers and the doctrine does not speak to the ruler's role.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Mercantilism sought a unified, state-directed economy and strong central power, so keeping territory by force is inferred as acceptable.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Colbertism worked to standardize regulations and trade rules under the crown, so distinct regional systems cut against the doctrine; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine-right monarchy was common in the era but is not part of the economic doctrine, and Mun's tract does not invoke it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income taxes did not exist; mercantilist fiscal policy centred on tariffs and monopolies, so nothing can be inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: An economic doctrine with no stated view of human nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Colbertism operated within absolute monarchy, so the crown's power over law is inferred, though English mercantilists like Mun lived under a more limited monarchy.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine's drive for colonies and trade routes might be read as supportive, but this is too uncertain to call.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; mercantilist states had varied constitutions.

leader-cult.rationale: Not addressed; royal glorification accompanied Colbert's France but is not part of the doctrine.

equal-parenting.rationale: A family-law question outside the doctrine's scope.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its view of the nation's wealth and power as a common interest ordered by the state.

land-redistribution.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its state-regulated, property-holding order.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilists; no clear position can be inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not addressed; mercantilist expansion aimed at trade and colonies, not co-ethnic claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilist economic writers; no clear position can be inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilist economic writers; no clear position can be inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from its focus on national bullion stocks and a favourable balance of trade, which separate national money serves.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from its competitive, zero-sum view of rival states.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its centralising state control, as in Colbertism.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilists; no clear position can be inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred from its treatment of wealth, trade balances and production as the basis of state power.

ban-cartels.rationale: Mercantilist states granted monopolies and chartered companies and regulated industry.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from its view that the state should steer and support national industry and trading firms.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed by mercantilists; no clear position can be inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the era's hierarchical, male-led state order.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Mercantilism sought colonies as monopoly suppliers and markets, closed by tariffs and navigation laws, aiming at export surplus and self-sufficiency.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its aim of cheap production and export surplus.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from its pursuit of national wealth through trade rather than a morally driven economy.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from its support for ordered state authority, which opposed revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from its development in monarchical, aristocratic early modern states.

missingStatements.text: A country should aim to export more than it imports.
missingStatements.rationale: Mun says to sell more to strangers yearly than is consumed of theirs, so the surplus returns as treasure, and the aim is central across mercantilist writing.

notes: Mercantilism was not a single system; writers addressed separate problems and some scholars reject the label. French practice was far more regulated than British. Answers on modern topics are inferences.
